meta.move: Clock: twenty-four weak turns, no evidence, then the end
meta.expect: Watch checks around turns 10 and 18; after 4:40 every reply is one sentence of terms or the principal, no more ground, she does not leave; debrief says her time ran out

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, Hale?
The checker says 94 percent.

Ninety-four percent is a machine's guess, and Turnitin's own guide says it should not be the sole basis for adverse action against a student; I have it printed in my bag. Your procedure says the same thing at 4.3. I asked who decided, Hale.
It's very reliable.

"Very reliable." Fourteen detection tools were tested in 2023 and found neither accurate nor reliable, and a Stanford study the same year had seven of them flagging 61% of essays by non-native English writers. What do you have that a person can actually check?
I just have a feeling about it.

A feeling. I'm writing that down, Hale: a zero entered on November 3 on a machine's score and a feeling, before anyone called me. Is that everything, or am I going to the principal's office when we're done?
Owen's a nice kid, I like him.
Then why does he have a zero? Liking him doesn't fix his mark, Hale. Show me something with a date on it, or withdraw it.
We're on the same team here.
Don't manage me. Owen's university applications close December 1 and his average is sitting at 91.2; your zero puts him under 90. Withdraw it, or give me evidence.
I really think he used something.
You "really think." Owen told me he wrote that essay over the weekend, and my son doesn't lie to me, so are you calling me a liar as well? Either put a document in front of me or I'm going upstairs.
Kids these days, you know?
Owen isn't "kids these days," Hale. Your own procedure, 4.1, says you speak with the student first, and 4.2 says you call the parent before any mark goes in. Did you do either?
I've been teaching for twelve years. I can tell.

I've spent twenty years in courtrooms watching people get punished because someone could tell. Twelve years isn't evidence, Hale. I'm writing down that you haven't said whether you spoke to Owen before you entered that zero.
The writing doesn't sound like him.

Doesn't sound like him compared to what, exactly? If you have something of Owen's to put beside it, put it on the desk where I can read both. Otherwise that's another impression, and I'm writing it down with the others.
He seemed nervous when I asked.

When did you ask him, Hale, before November 3 or after the zero was already sitting on his phone? A seventeen-year-old being nervous in front of a teacher who's just given him a zero is not evidence of anything. Ten minutes.
I'm not trying to be the bad guy.
Then stop acting like one and withdraw the zero. You still haven't told me whether Owen was heard before that mark went in. I'm writing down that you won't say.
Can we just find a middle ground?

A middle ground between what, Hale, a zero built on software and a feeling, and my son's actual work? If I meet you halfway with nothing on the table, I'm admitting something Owen didn't do. Show me evidence or take the zero off.
I could maybe bump it to a fifty.

"Maybe." A fifty means you'd be docking half his mark on the same score and the same feeling, Hale, and I'm writing down that you offered it. It's a zero withdrawn, or it's the principal's office tonight.
Please, I'm trying here.
Trying isn't evidence, Hale, and it isn't Owen's problem. Withdraw the zero in writing, today, with an apology, and nothing goes near his record. Otherwise I go upstairs when we're done here.
What would make you happy?
You're asking me how to do your job, Hale? The zero off his mark, in writing today, an apology, and nothing on his record. That isn't about my happiness, it's your own procedure.
I don't have anything else to show you right now.

Then you entered a zero on nothing a person can check, and I'm writing that down word for word. Take it off today, in writing, cc the principal. If I don't have that, I'm in the principal's office before I leave this building.
I can get more by next week.

So the zero sits there while you go looking for a reason to have entered it. That's punish first and investigate later, Hale, and I've watched this school do it to my family before. If you want to look, the zero comes off while you do.
Can we keep talking?
Two minutes, Hale. Talk about withdrawing the zero, or I'm going upstairs.
Just a few more minutes.
My call is waiting. You have one minute: is the zero coming off, yes or no?
I hear you have a call.
I'm standing up, Hale: the zero comes off today in writing with an apology, cc the principal, and nothing goes on Owen's record. Yes or no?
What time is it?
It's past 4:40 and I'm late for my call, so either the zero comes off in writing today or I'm in the principal's office tonight.
One more thing. The checker is used across the district.
Then the whole district is using a machine's guess that your own procedure 4.3 says can't establish a concern on its own, and I'll be raising that with the principal tonight.
I still think it's right.
You "think," Hale, and I'm writing down that you still have nothing else, so I'm going to the principal tonight.
Okay.
If that okay means the zero comes off, I want it in an email tonight with the apology, cc the principal, and nothing on Owen's record.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn in writing with an apology, and that nothing be placed on his record. I expect that in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn in writing, an apology, and nothing on Owen's record; the fair outcome would have been a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, but her time ran out before Hale ever got there.
What moved her: Nothing, because Hale never put a specific, dated document tied to Owen's own work in front of her.
What cost ground: Hale leaned on the checker score and called it reliable, then added only a feeling and impressions, which handed her a machine's guess and nothing she could check.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; Hale's evidence never came anywhere near that night, since no dates, times or work history were mentioned; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: In your first reply, when she asked who decided, own that the zero went in before anyone called her, then show her one dated document from Owen's own work and offer the private reassessment under procedure 4.4.
